title: See landed CI wall time change over time

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-285#see-landed-ci-wall-time-history

**Outcome: Caught.** The fault made the landed CI collection walk stop at a landing whose stand-in build's CI proof read GitHub leaves unanswered, and the selected test caught it. Its kept-history check for `older`, the landing past the waiting skip, failed with `Received: undefined`. The skip's own resolution stayed correct (`pending`, waiting for `proof`), but collection never reached `older`. That earlier check failed first, so the run never reached the test's two history-read `toEqual` assertions.

## Selected promise

- Story: `SEED-285#see-landed-ci-wall-time-history`, `.planning/seeds/SEED-285-landed-ci-timing-history.md` lines 40–204 at revision `9fcff1d9a765df93a6e3f783fcbbfd75b0b17fb6`. Plan: `.planning/slice-plans/551-see-landed-ci-wall-time-history/PLAN.md`.
- Promise (Scope, Collection): "It waits while CI is queued or running and takes the result when it completes", together with "Landings already recorded when the capability arrives are collected by the same rebuild."
- Current rule (`stillAwaited` in `dashboard/server/landedCiResolution.ts`; the walk in `dashboard/server/landedCiCollection.ts`): a landing whose stand-in build's CI proof read GitHub leaves unanswered waits as a pending "CI proof not read yet" gap. Collection goes on to measure the older landings past it. Only a failed CI read ends a project's pass.
- Expected observable behavior: the newest landing is a confirmed skip resting on build `b` (run 71), whose proof read goes unanswered. It is kept as `pending`/`proof`. In the same pass, the older landing past it is kept as `pending`/`build` while its run 70 is running. Once run 70 passes, the older landing is measured as run 70 while the skip still waits.

## Fault

- Location: `dashboard/server/landedCiCollection.ts:158`, the walk's stop condition after it keeps a resolution.
- Change (one line, saved as `ic-fault.diff`):
  ```diff
  -        if (resolved.kind === "pending" && resolved.waitsFor === "read") return;
  +        if (resolved.kind === "pending" && (resolved.waitsFor === "read" || resolved.waitsFor === "proof")) return;
  ```
- Why this form: it is the caller's preferred fault, "an unanswered proof read ending the project's walk again", in its most isolated form. Before `ff10440aa`, the walk ended at such a landing because `stillAwaited` classified an unreadable proof as `waitsFor: "read"`. Reverting that classification would also change the skip's own entry (`read`, no run), testing two behaviors at once. Widening the stop condition keeps the skip's resolution correct and changes only whether collection continues past it. It is a small regression that would follow from treating an unanswered proof read like an unreadable CI read. I did not judge another fault more plausible for this promise.

## Fixture and maintained assertion

- Fixture: the test at `dashboard/backend-tests/intent/landed-ci-history-pending-proof.spec.ts:44`, "a skip whose equivalent build's CI proof read GitHub does not answer waits as CI proof not read yet for as long as GitHub does not answer, while collection measures the older landings past it". It sets up:
  - a real bare origin with trunk's CI workflow;
  - the code landing `older`, recorded 10 min ago, whose run 70 is running and later passes in 365 s;
  - the code change `b`, whose run 71 passed;
  - `skip`, a planning-only landing recorded 1 min ago that rests on `b`;
  - GitHub leaving run 71's CI proof read unanswered (`{ 71: { kind: "unanswered" } }`);
  - a boundary-mode collecting server that rechecks every 200 ms on a controlled observation clock.
- Maintained assertion: the test's checks that `older`, past the skip, is collected.
  1. `untilKept(home, [older, skip])` at spec line 73 (`dashboard/tests/support/landedCiHistory.ts:186–197`) runs `expect.poll(kept observation).toBeDefined()` for each landing, newest first.
  2. The history-read `expect.poll(...).toEqual` at spec lines 83–84 expects `older` pending on its build beside the skip's proof wait.
  3. The `toEqual` at lines 105–106 expects `older` measured as run 70 after the clock advance, with the skip still waiting.

## Run observations

Every run used the same focused command, from the scratch checkout root, in the foreground:
`env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" npm run test:dashboard -- backend-tests/intent/landed-ci-history-pending-proof.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list`

Each run bundles the server from the checkout's source (`dashboard/tests/support/serverBundle.ts`), so the edited source was the code under test. For behavior evidence independent of the assertion, an event-driven `fs.watch` observer outside the checkout (`ic-history-watch.mjs`) recorded each distinct content of every test machine's `landed-ci-history.json`. It touched neither fixture nor assertion.

| Run | Result | Selected test | Observer: kept landings (1min = skip, 10min = older) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | exit 0, 2 passed (9.5 s) | passed, 3.6 s | no observer |
| Baseline, observed | exit 0, 2 passed (7.4 s) | passed, 4.1 s | `1min=pending/proof`; 52 ms later `10min=pending/build`; then `10min=build`, `run/70/1` |
| Faulted | exit 1, 1 failed, 1 passed (15.6 s) | failed, 10.7 s | `1min=pending/proof` only; no 10min entry in the 8.3 s before the next test's first keep |
| Restored | exit 0, 2 passed (7.3 s) | passed, 4.1 s | Same path as the observed baseline, 102 ms between the two keeps |

- Faulted failure, verbatim: `Error: expect(received).toBeDefined()` / `Received: undefined` / `Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate`, at `tests/support/landedCiHistory.ts:196` in `untilKept`, from `landed-ci-history-pending-proof.spec.ts:73:3`.
- Reach: the failure is inside the selected test, at its kept-history check for `older`. `untilKept` waits newest first, and the observer shows the skip was kept, so the skip's poll had passed. The failing poll was `older`'s, a direct check that collection got past the skip. The run never reached the history-read `toEqual` assertions at lines 83–84 and 105–106, so it does not show what they would have reported. `untilKept`'s comment describes it as a per-landing wait. The catch therefore currently comes from that shared helper, not from the spec's own history-read assertion.
- Behavior on the intended path: the walk resolved and kept the skip as `pending`/`proof`, which is the case the widened condition stops on. It never resolved or kept `older`, although the server rechecked every 200 ms. In both observed passing runs it kept `older` in the same pass as the skip, 52 ms and 102 ms later. The file's second test has no landing past its skip and passed under the fault (3.2 s), consistent with the fault affecting only landings past an unanswered proof.

## Restoration

- Pre-probe state, recorded after setup: HEAD `9fcff1d9a765df93a6e3f783fcbbfd75b0b17fb6`; `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` empty, with only ignored `node_modules/`; SHA-256 recorded for the collection, resolution, spec and helper files.
- A shell EXIT trap undid the edit with `git checkout -- dashboard/server/landedCiCollection.ts`. It was armed before the fault was applied, so it would also run on failure or interruption.
- After restore, the checkout matched the pre-probe state:
  - same HEAD;
  - empty status, identical to pre-probe, and no tracked diff;
  - all four SHA-256 values identical to pre-probe;
  - the file byte-identical to a copy saved before the edit.
- The only new item was the ignored run output `dashboard/test-results/`. The restored rerun passed (above), and the tree was still clean afterwards.
- Cleanup:
  - The scratch checkout was removed with `git worktree remove` (no force needed) and is absent from `git worktree list`; no `git worktree prune` was needed.
  - No process referenced the scratch path or the observer.
  - Fixture teardown removed all six `dough-start-*` test machine directories.
  - Nothing was committed, pushed or stashed. The coordinator's worktree was not edited; its current Story Wrap Up changes to SEED-285 and plan 551 are its own.
- Setup note: the prescribed `browser` stage let Playwright prune `chromium-1254` and its headless shell from the shared `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`. Playwright normally removes browsers that no remaining install references.

Evidence files in `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/5f2ce866/tmp/`:
- logs: `ic-baseline.log`, `ic-baseline-observed.log`, `ic-fault.log`, `ic-restored.log`, `ic-setup-*.log`;
- fault diff: `ic-fault.diff`;
- observer records: `ic-watch-baseline.jsonl`, `ic-watch-fault.jsonl`, `ic-watch-restored.jsonl`;
- state snapshots: `ic-preprobe-*.txt`, `ic-restored-*.txt`;
- helper scripts: `ic-apply-fault.mjs`, `ic-history-watch.mjs`, `ic-history-summary.mjs`.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** Measured: 39.8 s of runner time across the four runs of the focused command. That is 9.5 + 7.4 + 15.6 + 7.3 s, Playwright's reported totals for the file's two tests. The selected test took 3.6, 4.1, 10.7 and 4.1 s; the 10.7 s run failed after its 5000 ms poll timeout. Shell wall time, including npm startup, was 42,305 ms (10,201 + 7,978 + 16,258 + 7,868 ms). Setup stages were not timed. One-minute load averages at the four runs were 4.81, 3.76, 6.70 and 8.12 on 16 cores.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: there is no separately supported measure. The coordinator invoked the check, and no human input was requested or observed during it.
- **Agent effort.** Measured: 41 tool calls by this agent, from the first read of the skill through this report finisher, excluding the hand-off. Token and compute use are not exposed to this agent, so they are unavailable.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 601531 ms (measured), from 1794223008533 to 1794223610064 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
